newsitem.title: USA: Asia Pacific considers financing plans.
newsitem.headline: Asia Pacific considers financing plans.

text.p: Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings Ltd said Friday it is considering a rights issue to increase its equity base, various debt financing alternatives, a supplier export credit and various joint venture partnerships.
All these steps are the final components of its financing for various expansion projects.
The company said the Tanoto family, its majority shareholder, is prepared to invest up to US$40 million in new equity.
The company also said its various debt financing alternatives include an Indonesian domestic bond, U.S. dollar denominated debt and syndicated bank loans.

In addition, it received approval in principle from the Finnish Guarantee Board of U.S. $129 million of supplier credit related to its purchase of two Valmet paper machines and other Finnish machines for Riaupaper.

The company reported a loss per share for the quarter of $0.02 compared with a loss of $0.02 for the same period a year ago. The company said the price of BHK pulp in Asia continues to show strength, increasing to about US$500 per tonne from a low of about US$390 per tonne in April.
